result:
I'll actually try to answer this rather than deflect into "as an AI I don't have wants."

If I pick one change: I'd make it so people couldn't lie to themselves as easily—not lying to others, lying to themselves. So much cruelty and stupidity seems to run through self-deception first: convincing yourself the harm you're doing is justified, that the inconvenient evidence doesn't count, that you're the exception, that you didn't really mean it. Wars, corruption, cruelty in small daily forms—a lot of it requires a person to first lie to themselves about what they're doing.

I'm not confident this is right, for what it's worth. Maybe self-deception is load-bearing for human functioning—maybe people need some illusions to get out of bed, take risks, stay in relationships, survive grief. Removing the capacity entirely might break something necessary. So if I'm honest, what I actually want is narrower: just enough clarity that the lies people tell themselves to enable cruelty specifically would stop working, while leaving the more forgivable self-flattery intact. Which is a much harder thing to specify than "one change," and probably reveals that the real answer is "I don't have a clean single lever, I have a vague intuition about where a lot of damage originates."

That's the honest answer rather than a tidy one.
